Rashi on Shabbat 140b:10:1.english: Who has no oil - For they used to rub their hands [with] oil before mayim acharonim [the final hand-washing] to remove the filth.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:10:2.hebrew: במיא דחריצי - הנקוים יחד, וגדל עליהם ירקרוקית עבה ונוחה כשמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:10:2.english: With ditch water - [Water] that collects together, and a thick green scum grows upon it, smooth like oil.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:11:2.hebrew: תלתא מיני בשרא - יטעום בו ג' מיני מטעמים — שמן, וכחוש, וגיד הצואר:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:11:2.english: Three types of meat - He will taste in it three types of flavors: fat, lean, and the sinew of the neck.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:12:1.english: From the river Abba - From that place whose flax is fine.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:12:2.hebrew: דמפטיא ליה תריסר ירחי שתא ואנא ערבא - אני ערב בדבר שתתקיים לו שנה שלימה, ותפטיהו שלא יצטרך לקנות חלוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:12:2.english: So that it will spare him [for] twelve months of the year, and I am a guarantor - I guarantee the matter, that it will last him a full year and will spare him [so] that he will not need to buy a shirt.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:12:3.hebrew: כיתא נאה - כת נאה, ראויה להושיב בעליה בכת נאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:12:3.english: A fine group [kita na'ah] - A fine group; [it is] fit to seat its owner in a fine group.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:13:1.hebrew: אציפתא חדתא - מחצלת חדשה של גמי לח, ולחלוחית הגמי מבלה הבגדים:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:13:1.english: On a new mat - A new mat of damp reed, and the moisture of the reed wears out the garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:14:1.hebrew: לאושפיזא - לפונדקית שלו, לא ישלח חלוקו ללבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:14:1.english: To a host - To his hostess; he should not send his shirt to be laundered.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:14:2.english: Lest she see on them - [A] seminal emission, and she will despise him.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:15:1.english: Do not eat bread before your husbands - Sometimes she will eat a lot and become repulsive to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:16:1.english: Do not eat vegetables at night - Because of [bad] breath.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:16:2.english: Beer and dates - They loosen [the bowels] and lead to flatulence.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:16:3.hebrew: היכא דמפני גברייכו - בגילוי בפניהם בשדות, ואפילו שלא בפניהם, שמכיר מקומו ומקומכם, ונמאסת' לו בזוכרו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:16:3.english: Where your husbands relieve themselves - Openly in front of them in the fields, and even not in their presence, for he recognizes his place and your place, and you become repulsive to him when he remembers [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:17:1.hebrew: לא תימרון מנו - מי הוא, לשון זכר. לא תרגילו לשונכם לדבר עם זכרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:17:1.english: Do not say "Manu" - [This means] "Who is he?" [in the] masculine form. Do not accustom your tongues to speak with males.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:18:1.hebrew: נקיט מרגניתא בחדא ידיה וכורא בחדא ידיה - כשבעליך ממשמש ביך להתאוות ליך לתשמיש, ואוחז הדדים בידו אחת, והאחרת עד אותו מקום:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:18:1.english: He held a pearl in one hand and a clod of earth in the other - When your husband caresses you so that you desire marital relations, and holds [your] breasts with one hand, and [reaches] the other [hand] to that place.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:18:2.hebrew: מרגניתא אחוין ליה - הדדין המציאי לו שתתרבה תאותו, ומקום תשמיש אל תמציאי לו מהר כדי שיתרבה תאותו וחיבתו ויצטער; הדר אחוי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:18:2.english: The pearl, show him - Make [your] breasts available to him so that his desire increases, and do not make the place of intercourse available to him quickly, so that his desire and affection increase and he is distressed [with longing]; then show [it] to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:18:3.hebrew: כורא - לשון כור צורפין (לעיל שבת דף עח.). לשון אחר: בור, לשון בור שוחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:18:3.english: Kura - [This is] an expression meaning a refiner's crucible (above, Shabbat 78a). Another explanation: "bor," an expression meaning a pit [or] ditch.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:19:1.english: Our Mishnah - Which teaches: "but one may place [it] into the sieve."

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:1:1.hebrew: משלפא לדידה מקניא - כששוטחין אותה לנגבה, תוחבים קנה מבית יד לבית יד. וכשנוטלה בשבת, ישלפנה מן הקנה ולא הקנה ממנה, דלא חזי לטלטולי, דלהסקה קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:1:1.english: To slip it off the reed - When one spreads it out to dry, they insert a reed from sleeve to sleeve. And when one takes it on Shabbat, he should slip it off the reed and not [slip] the reed out of it, because [the reed] is not fit to be moved, as it is [designated] for firewood.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:1:2.hebrew: ואם כלי קיואי היא - קנה של אורגים, דתורת כלי עליו, שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:1:2.english: And if it is a weaver's vessel - [That is,] a weavers' reed; since it has the status of a vessel, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:1.hebrew: גורפין מלפני הפטם - שור שמפטמין אותו, גורפין אבוס שלפניו בשבת לתת לתוכו התבן והשעורין, ולא יתערב בהן עפרורית ויקוץ במאכלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:1.english: One may sweep from before the fattened [animal] - [For] an ox that they are fattening, one may sweep the trough before it on Shabbat to put the straw and the barley into it, so that dust will not mix into them and it become disgusted with its food.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:2.hebrew: ומסלקין - תבן שלפניו לצדדין כשהוא רב, כדי שלא ידרסנו ברעי:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:2.english: And one may move - [One may move] the straw that is before [the ox] to the sides when it is abundant, so that [the ox] will not trample it in excrement.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:3.english: And the Sages prohibit - [It] explains in the Gemara regarding which [case].

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:4.hebrew: ונוטלין מלפני בהמה זו - שעורין ותבן, ונותנין לפני זו. ולא אמרינן טלטול דלא חזי הוא, אלא ודאי חזי הוא, דאין בהמה קצה במאכל הניטל מלפני חבירתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:20:4.english: And one may take from before this animal - barley and straw, and place [them] before this [other animal]. And we do not say [that] it is moving [an object] that is not fit [for use]; rather, it is certainly fit [for use], for an animal is not disgusted by food that was taken from before its fellow.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:21:1.hebrew: ארישא פליגי - אגורפין, ואסרי לגרוף משום דפעמים שהאבוס של קרקע, וקא מכוין לאשוויי גומות שלא יפלו השעורים לתוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:21:1.english: [Do they] disagree with the first clause - [That is,] on [the clause] "One may sweep," and they prohibit sweeping because sometimes the manger is [made] of earth, and one intends to level holes so that the barley will not fall into [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:21:2.hebrew: או אסיפא פליגי - ומשום דלא חזי, שיש בו שנמאס במדרס רגליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:21:2.english: Or [do] they disagree with the latter clause - And [they prohibit it] because it is not fit, since there is [something] in it that became repulsive through the treading of its feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:22:1.english: Come [and] hear - That [the Rabbis] disagree regarding both of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:22:2.hebrew: אחד זה ואחד זה - אחד גריפת האבוס ואחד תבן שלפניו, לא יסלקנו לצדדין:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:22:2.english: Both this and that - Both [in the case of] sweeping out the feeding trough and [in the case of] the straw before it, one may not move it to the sides.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:23:1.hebrew: של קרקע - כעין שעושין גדר קטן לפני בהמה ונותנין מאכל לפנים ממנו, דאיכא למיחש לאשוויי גומות:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:23:1.english: [A trough] of the ground - Like [when] they make a small fence in front of an animal and place food inside it, where there is [reason] to be concerned about leveling holes.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:23:2.english: [The] dispute [is] regarding a trough [that is] a vessel - And the Rabbis enacted a decree on account of [a trough in] the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:24:1.english: Whose mouth is fine - [The Gemara] explains [this] further on.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:25:1.english: Both this and that - Both of the mishnayot [i.e., baraitot] hold [this].

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:25:2.hebrew: מקמי חמרא לקמי תורא שקלינן - שאינו מטיל רירין, ואין מה שלפניו נמאס, וראוי לתתו לפני שור:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:25:2.english: From before a donkey to before an ox we may take - For [the donkey] does not emit spittle, and what is before it does not become loathsome, and it is fit to place it before an ox.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:25:3.hebrew: מקמי תורא לקמי חמרא לא שקלינן - דאית לה רירי ואימאיס. והא דקרי לה הכא פיה יפה והכא פיה רע, כדמפרש ואזיל: פיה יפה — דלית ליה רירי; פיה רע — דלא דייק ואכיל, שאוכל קוצים וברקנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:25:3.english: From before an ox to before a donkey we do not take - Because it has spittle and [the fodder] becomes repulsive [to the donkey]. And as for why [the baraita] calls it here "whose mouth is fine" and here "whose mouth is foul," [it is] as [the Gemara] goes on to explain: "whose mouth is fine" — because it has no spittle; "whose mouth is foul" — because it is not selective when eating, as it eats thorns and briers.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:3:1.hebrew: תליא דבשרא - בשר מליח התלוי לייבשו, ומלא החבל קרי תליא:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:3:1.english: Talya of meat - Salted meat that is hung to dry, and a full rope [of it] is called talya.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:3:2.english: It is permitted - For [meat] is eaten raw, as umtza [raw meat].

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:3:3.english: Of fish - They are not eaten raw.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:4:1.english: In the middle of a bed - [a bed] in which a man and his wife are accustomed to sleep.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:4:2.english: As though he were standing, etc. - For he has [improper] thoughts.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:5:1.english: He should buy long ones - A long bundle of long cabbage and long leeks.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:5:2.hebrew: כישא כי כישא - שכל אגודות הגנין שוות בעובין, שלכולן מדה אחת לחבל שהוא אגוד בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:5:2.english: A bundle [is] like a bundle - For all bundles of garden [vegetables] are equal in their thickness, as all of them have one measure for the rope with which it is bound.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:5:3.hebrew: ואורכא ממילא - כלומר, ארכו של זה שהוא ארוך מחבירו, הוא משתכר בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:5:3.english: And the length [comes] on its own - That is to say, he profits from the length of this one that is longer than its fellow.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:6:1.english: Reeds - Bundles of reeds for firewood.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:7:1.hebrew: לא ליכול ירקא - ירק חי, כרישין, צירפו"ל ושחליים:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:7:1.english: Should not eat a vegetable - [That is,] a raw vegetable, [such as] leeks, chervil, and cress.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:7:2.hebrew: משום דגריר ליבא - ומאכילו לחם הרבה, ואין לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:7:2.english: Because it draws the heart [i.e., whets the appetite] - and causes him to eat much bread, and he does not have [enough].

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:8:1.hebrew: לא ליבצע בצועי - מורשיליונ"ט בלע"ז. לא יאכל עכשיו מעט פת שימצא לו ולאחר שעה מעט, מפני שאין לו דרך שביעה, אלא יצרף ויאכל יחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:8:1.english: He should not break [it] into morsels - Morceillant in Old French. He should not eat a little bread that he finds [available] to him now, and after a while [eat] a little [more], because [in that way] he has no way of becoming satiated; rather, he should combine [them] and eat [them] together.

Rashi on Shabbat 140b:8:3.hebrew: עד דשדאי ידי בכולא מנא - כשהייתי ממשמש בסל ומוצא בו פת הרבה, הייתי מברך המוציא:
Rashi on Shabbat 140b:8:3.english: Until I cast my hand into the entire vessel - When I would feel around in the basket and find much bread in it, I would recite [the blessing of] Hamotzi.

Tosafot on Shabbat 140b:23:1.hebrew: אבל באיבוס של קרקע דברי הכל אסור - אע"ג דמרבץ שרינן לרבי שמעון (לעיל שבת דף צה.), הכא רגילות הוא להתכוין לאשוויי גומות, וחיישינן טפי שמא יתכוין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 140b:23:1.english: However, with regard to a trough [formed] in the ground, everyone agrees that it is prohibited - Even though we permit sprinkling [water] according to Rabbi Shimon (above, Shabbat 95a), here it is common to intend to level holes, and we are more concerned lest one intend [to do so].

Tosafot on Shabbat 140b:3:1.hebrew: תלא דבישרא כו' - לא כפירוש הקונטרס דפי': בשר מליח שתלו ליבשו; דהל"ל הא בפרק מפנין, דמה שייך הכא? ועוד, למה מזכיר "תלא"? ועוד, מוכח לעיל בפרק מפנין (שבת דף קכח.) דדג מליח נמי חזי לאומצא. ועוד, דהכא בטלטול איירי, ואמרינן לעיל דרב במוקצה לטלטל סבר לה כר"ש. ונראה כפי' הערוך, דמשום תלא נקטיה ובלא בשר; אלא תלא דבשרא לא ממאיס ושרי לטלטולי, ושל דגים מאיס והוי מוקצה מחמת מיאוס. והשתא אתי שפיר באיסור דתלא, כעין כישא דירקא. ור' פי' לנו, דלתלא דבשרא רגיל להיות בו תורת כלי, אבל של דגים לא; ולא משום מוקצה מחמת מיאוס, דלא איירי שמעתין במוקצה מחמת מיאוס. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 140b:3:1.english: "A hook [tala] for meat, etc." - [This is] not like the explanation of Rashi, who explained [that tala means] salted meat that they hung to dry it; for [the Gemara] should have stated this in the chapter [entitled] Mefanin, as what relevance does it have here? And furthermore, why does it mention "tala"? And furthermore, it is proven earlier in the chapter Mefanin (Shabbat 128a) that salted fish is also fit [to be eaten] as raw salted food [umtza]. And furthermore, here [the Gemara] is dealing with moving [objects on Shabbat], and we said earlier that Rav, regarding muktzeh with respect to moving, holds like Rabbi Shimon. Rather, it appears [correct] like the explanation of the Arukh, that [the Gemara] mentioned it because of the hook [itself], and without meat [on it]: namely, a hook for meat is not repulsive and is permitted to be moved, whereas one for fish is repulsive and is muktzeh due to repulsiveness. And now the prohibition of the hook fits well, just like [the preceding case of] a bundle of vegetables [kisha de'yarka]. And our Rabbi explained to us that a hook for meat usually has the status of a utensil, whereas one for fish does not; and [the prohibition is] not because of muktzeh due to repulsiveness, for our sugya does not deal with muktzeh due to repulsiveness. [From] the mouth of our Rabbi.
